result.topic_en: Gauss studies the cubic $t^3 - tt + (\omega-\tfrac14)t + \omega = 0$ associated with the condition $\alpha\beta\gamma\delta\varepsilon = 4\omega$ (likely the pentagramma mirificum), relates its roots, computes a numerical example for $m=4$, and derives angles and semi-axes.
result.transcription:
$\alpha\beta\gamma\delta\varepsilon = 4\omega$

$t^3 - tt + (\omega - \frac{1}{4})t + \omega = 0$
Ist eine Wurzel $= t^0$, die beiden andern $t', t''$ so wird
$t^0 + t' = \frac{1}{4(t^0-1)(t'-1)}$
$2t' = \sqrt{\frac{(t^0t^0 + t^0 - 1)t^0}{t^0-1}} - t^0 + 1$
Soll $t' = mt^0$ werden, so ist
$\{(2m+1)t^0 - 1\}^2 (t^0-1) = (t^0t^0 + t^0 - 1)t^0$
$4m(m+1).t^{0\,3} - 4(m+1)^2.t^0t^0 + 4(m+1)t^0 - 1 = 0$

methods.what: Cubic equation governing the configuration with product condition
Relation between two roots of the cubic
Expression of a second root in terms of the first
Condition t'=m t^0 reduces to a cubic in t^0
Third root from the sum of roots
Numerical solution for m=4 with three root sets and logarithms
Symmetric special solution and parametrization of the quantities
Semi-axes represented as arcs whose tangents are given

items.english: This has three real roots; but since $t'' = 1-(1+m)t^0$ (for positive $m$) must become negative so that $\omega$ can be positive, only one is usable.
